title: Listening to his own recordings: Something for Liza and Mambo Blues
summary: Rowe plays two tracks, and Candoli identifies Al Cohn's tune and his own Mambo Blues, with Bob Cooper's last music.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well let me play something for you and get your opinion on this.
Oh, I know exactly what that is. It’s an Al Cohn tune with Osie Johnson on drums I think. No it’s Osie Johnson’s tune. Oh God I’m coming up on everything but the right one.
Well do you recognize the trumpet player?
Yeah I know it’s me. Oh, I know it’s me, but I’m trying to think, it’s either Al Cohn—
Okay, all right. It’s Al Cohn’s tune, and I forget what he calls that.
“Something for Liza” sure. Okay that’s on VSOP. You know what, he sent me some of those CD’s and I kind of like it. I mean it’s almost like what I’m doing today but it’s a little different.
You had your own tune on it.
That’s some good stuff right there.

You know what I’m glad you like it because I hadn’t heard that in a long time and I forgot about that tune. That was “Mambo Blues” huh? Because VSOP put out an album of Bob Cooper and I. It was a live broadcast we did for KLON, a jazz station in Long Beach. And it was Bob Cooper’s last music before he died, about a couple of months. And VSOP put it out on a CD. I wish I had that with me. I’ll have to send you that.
